name: Orison Brushed Flannel Shirt
description:
Orison is a workwear-adjacent label that occupies the comfortable middle ground between functional and presentable — the kind of brand that outfitters stock alongside hiking gear and hardware stores carry alongside work gloves. The Brushed Flannel Shirt is a long-sleeve button-front in a medium-weight brushed flannel, cut generously through the shoulders and chest to allow movement without pulling. The plaid pattern runs in a traditional block check — a rotation of four colorways each season, always including a dark red/black and a navy/forest green. Two chest pockets with button flaps. A slightly curved hem that can be worn tucked or untucked.

This shirt has no technology in it. It is flannel. It is warm in the way flannel is warm — not aggressively, not technically, just reliably. People wear it open over a thermal layer on job sites, or buttoned up to the second button at a casual dinner, or thrown over a tank top on a cool morning before the temperature decides what it wants to be. It is the kind of shirt that appears in the background of every social tier from Tier 2 through Tier 3 without calling attention to itself. That is its entire point.
what_it_says: You don't overthink it. You put on a flannel shirt because it's a good flannel shirt.
worn_by: anyone who needs a reliable layer
story_hooks: A specific Orison flannel — dark red/black check, 2197 season — has appeared in three separate missing persons case files, worn by three different people, in three different locations across the corridor.
Orison's flannel fabric is woven by a single contracted mill that has just been purchased by a corponation that has no interest in continuing textile production.
Someone wearing an Orison flannel turns out to be significantly more dangerous than the shirt suggested — which was, in retrospect, the point.
